newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, positive trend seen intact.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, positive trend seen intact.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.4 percent on Thursday in what market participants said was a technical correction after recent gains but traders said the market was likely to resume its upward trend next week.
The SBI index fell 5.13 points to 1,277.8. Overall eight shares fell, seven rose, two were unchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover fell to 224.6 million tolars from 557.7 million.

"There has to be a technical correction sometimes but there are still plenty of foreign and domestic investors in the market so shares should start rising slowly, if not on Friday then next week," said Karmen Korbun, a trader at Creditanstalt.

She added, however, that the rise was not expected to be as strong as last week. From January 7 to January 13, the SBI share-index rose 12.8 percent, backed by foreign buying of newly privatised companies, before retreating two percent.
Drug company Lek's issue A was the most actively traded share, rising two percent to 25,000 on volume of 4,434 shares for total turnover of 110.8 million tolars.
Food company Droga was the leading decliner, closing 2.98 percent lower at 25,100 on volume of seven shares for total turnover of 0.2 million tolars.
Construction company GPG was the top gainer, rising 9.24 percent to 7,450 in just one trade.
